scenarios.title: #US0.04 #US0.01 #US0.02 #US0.06 AC1 a customer of the bank submits an application for one loan and gets back its identifier, a Location and the amount in whole cents
#US0.04 #US0.02 #US0.03 AC2 a caller without the right to submit an application is refused with the refusal code, and no application is recorded
#US0.05 AC3 the submission is published once, as an integration event carrying the application identifier, in the same transaction that records it

amendments.subject: scenario "#US0.05 AC3 the submission is published once, as an integration event carrying the application identifier, in the same transaction that records it"
amendments.reason: AC3 asks for one integration event carrying the application identifier, published once. The locked scenario called `submitted.recorded()`, a method the EventRecorder does not have, so it could not typecheck or run; the current `submitted.received()` is the recorder's method for the events received so far, in order, which is what the scenario meant. The assertions are unchanged (exactly one event, `applicationId` equal to the response identifier), so the new version is not weaker; the transactional part of AC3 is asserted in neither version, which the owner may want to cover later.

amendments.subject: scenario "#US0.04 #US0.01 #US0.02 #US0.06 AC1 a customer of the bank submits an application for one loan and gets back its identifier, a Location and the amount in whole cents"
amendments.reason: AC1 asks that a customer of the bank submits one application and gets back its identifier, a Location and the amount in whole cents. The locked version posted without the customer being a customer (no `self` relation), so it could not pass, and the new `relate` of `customer:customer-1#self@user:customer-1` only supplies that precondition, as the arrangement the rights decision needs; the body, the 201 status, the Location pattern and the amount assertions are unchanged, so the new version is no weaker.
